newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghans say Taleban headquarters town falls.
newsitem.headline: Afghans say Taleban headquarters town falls.

text.p: The Taleban front line town of Jabal-os-Siraj at the mouth of the Salang Pass has fallen to the forces of former Afghan government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood, reliable Afghan sources said on Sunday.

They said the forces of purist Islamic Taleban militia which took Kabul just two weeks ago had retreated to the town of Charikar, a 30-minute drive south of Jabal-os-Saraj after it fell on Saturday evening.
The sources said Charikar came under attack on Sunday morning and it was not clear who held the town.
They were unable to give details of the fall of Jabal-os-Siraj, which had been the target of an attack by Masood's forces launched in the Salang Pass through the Hindu Kush mountains on Tuesday.
Masood has orchestrated a series of hit-and-run attacks between Jabal-os-Siraj and Kabul, 75 km (50 miles) to the south, over the past few days, including strikes on Charikar.
